newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt won't give in on handover laws - Patten.
newsitem.headline: HK govt won't give in on handover laws - Patten.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten on Wednesday opposed calls to allow a China-appointed lawmaking body to pass legislation on residency rights in the territory before it is handed back to China on July 1.
"That is our position, our position is not going to change," Patten told reporters at a public function.
Patten's comment followed a row this week after Beijing made a unilateral announcement on who would qualify for "right of abode" or permanent residency in Hong Kong after July 1.
Beijing plans to submit the bill before June 30 to the China-appointed provisional legislature, which will replace the elected chamber upon the handover.
The Hong Kong government on Monday slammed the plan and warned that if the bill were to be handled by the interim chamber before July 1, it would invite legal challenges.

Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp, which has been in the forefront of clashes with China over arrangements for handing the British colony back to China, opposes the interim chamber and has vowed to sue if it tries to pass laws before July 1.
Patten urged China to take up Hong Kong's earlier proposal to publish the bill for public consultation by the end of May or early June and have it enacted into law after the handover.
The right of abode issue is crucial for 750,000 Hong Kong people who have foreign citizenship but who still want to know whether they can keep their Hong Kong permanent residency after July 1.
